previous_action: Gaius Maximus Valerius expands his merchant connections and instructs his household and people living on his estates to mention his trade and road networks in ordinary conversation outside their work, seeking to make the network familiar beyond the estate itself.

continuity.campaign_development: In February 60 BCE, Valerius deliberately expanded his merchant connections and encouraged his household and estate residents to speak naturally of the roads, waterways, lake port and trade network outside their work. Independent merchants began treating the estate routes as one commercial corridor, while Roman political reports continued to arrive through the widening flow of merchants and messengers.
